releases.body: Fix npm-installed TUI reactivity by shipping Solid-compiled JSX. Application source is unchanged; compilation is a temporary packaging workaround until the upstream OpenCode/OpenTUI loader fix ships.

## Fixed

- Archives remain applied when switching models, even when model-specific messages disappear. Newly revealed messages remain visible.
- Nested archives and restored originals preserve captured membership and transcript order across compaction.
- Unidentified host messages remain visible without blocking archive ranges.
- The archive worker is explicitly instructed to return bare JSON.

## Added

- Unresolved archive blocks are shown in the footer and `/lacuna` status.

Existing archive state is not migrated.

Verified with 36 passing tests and TypeScript typechecking.

Context summaries are now written by a background archive agent forked from the main agent, instead of by the main agent inline.

The fork replays the captured request prefix verbatim, so the prompt cache is reused. It chooses its own ranges, and ready summaries replace the originals before the next request without any message or notification.

## Breaking

- `archive` takes no arguments; the archive agent selects what to summarise.
- `context_status` is removed.
- `nudgeAt` is removed. Use `archiveAt`.
- Archive calls in the old summary format are no longer rewritten.

## Added

- Automatic archiving past `archiveAt` (default `200000`), with a growth cooldown between attempts.
- TUI status: a footer spinner while a job runs, a composer strip, `/lacuna` for job details, and a marker for context updates not yet acknowledged by a response.

## Fixed

- Calibration anchors are per model, so switching models mid-session no longer corrupts the learned token factor.
- Footer stats are scoped to the session location, so another location cannot zero the archived figure.
- A failed background save no longer fails the request that triggered it.

Fixes the footer failing to load when installed from npm (`Cannot find package '@opentui/solid'`). The TUI peer dependencies `@opentui/core`, `@opentui/solid` and `solid-js` are now required, so npm installs them.
